chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It was narrated to me by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfali from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, who raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).
He said: 'One who makes something to boast about it, Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment with a black face.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for showing off in good deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this narration from Imam Ali (AS) via the chain of Sa'd ibn Abdullah emphasizes that *mufakhara* (boasting) corrupts the inner purity of deeds, resulting in a 'black face' as a physical manifestation of spiritual darkness. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia theology, where the face's color on the Day of Judgment serves as an external indicator of the soul's internal state of sincerity (*ikhlas*) versus vanity. The hadith thus serves as a critical reminder for believers to purify their intentions from the desire for worldly recognition.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ya’qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Ibrahim al-Nawfali from al-Hussain b. al-Mukhtar who raised it to Ameer al-Mumineen (a.s.)
who said: “One who makes something to boast about it will be raised on Qiyamat black-faced.”
